tldr: Anthropic's IPO triggered a rush to give retail investors local-currency, fractional access: CIBC is launching a Canadian Depositary Receipt and B3 a sub-R$100 BDR. Meanwhile, fintechs are moving into brokerage and bank licences (Kalshi, Mercado Pago, Nubank, Dave), and a US bank outage and the Mercado Bitcoin hack highlight reliability and security risk.
themes: Fintechs and exchanges becoming full-stack (brokerage, charters)
Cross-border expansion by Nubank, Mercado Pago and Kalshi
Outages and security incidents hitting trust

highlights.headline: CIBC will launch an Anthropic Canadian Depositary Receipt after the US IPO, and has added another CDR to reach 145 in its lineup
highlights.why: CIBC is a direct competitor and is using CDRs to give Canadians low-friction access to hot US listings. Simplii should check whether its self-directed investing offers CDRs, and how fast it can support new listings on IPO day.

highlights.headline: B3 launched an Anthropic BDR (ANTH34) for under R$100, trading at the same time as the Nasdaq debut
highlights.why: Same-day, low-ticket local access to a major US IPO is becoming the expectation. It is a template for how Simplii could offer fractional or CDR-style access to marquee listings.

highlights.headline: Kalshi is buying broker FB Securities to launch stock and ETF trading, and Mercado Pago now offers CEDEARs, including S&P 500 exposure, inside its payments app
highlights.why: Prediction-market and payments players are adding brokerage on top of existing user bases. That shows how easily non-bank apps can expand into investing and compete for the same wallets.

highlights.headline: Nubank gets Brazilian bank-charter approval via the Porto Real acquisition, Dave applies for a US bank charter, and Nubank US reaches all 50 states within weeks of launch
highlights.why: Digital-first challengers are securing charters and expanding across borders. Simplii should expect fintechs to offer a broader product set with deposit-grade trust, and to push into new markets quickly.
